blocks.text: # Pumpkin seed protein powder: what cold-pressed, finely milled and easy to mix actually tell you
blocks.verdict: editorial heading, interpretation, connective argument or proposed development approach; not an empirical test result

blocks.text: A pumpkin protein powder can be sold as a daily protein serving, a simple kitchen ingredient or a smooth addition to coffee and oatmeal. Those are different reasons to buy, even when the product names look almost identical. Our three Amazon detail-page examples illustrate all three approaches: Sprout Living emphasizes cold pressing and protein per serving; Anthony’s emphasizes uncomplicated kitchen use; Micro Ingredients connects fine milling with everyday versatility.[1][2][3]
semantic_review: Seller positioning and exact gallery label declaration; Blend conflict preserved, no physical composition verdict.
Seller kitchen positioning plus toasted/pressed/milled wording; 8g/5g/56 label versus 30 structured field; cold pressing not incompatible with prior toasting.
Seller everyday uses and approximately 30g/18g/30 label; raw/fine-milled not independently measured.

blocks.text: For a product developer, the useful question is not which phrase sounds most advanced. It is which promise the finished product needs to deliver. A powder that works in a blender smoothie has not thereby demonstrated rapid dispersion in a shaker or stability in a bottled drink. Pressing, milling and protein isolation describe different operations, while a mixing instruction describes use rather than a measured material property.[4][8]

blocks.text: **Anthony’s: a small recipe addition with a documented processing description.** The 5 g protein figure belongs to an 8 g tablespoon, not to the larger portions used by the other two brands. Its back pouch describes toasting the seeds, pressing out oil and finely milling the remaining pulp. The front also says “COLD-PRESSED.” Toasting and pressing describe different stages, so their coexistence is not automatically a contradiction; it does mean that cold-pressed should not be read as proof of an entirely unheated product. The actual discrepancy is the serving count: 30 in the original structured field versus 56 in the gallery. Neither a variant change nor a reformulation is established.[2]

blocks.text: ## Pressing removes oil; milling makes powder; isolation separates protein
blocks.verdict: editorial heading, interpretation, connective argument or proposed development approach; not an empirical test result

blocks.text: A supplier’s process description helps explain why “pumpkin protein” need not mean a purified protein isolate. Austrade describes its unroasted concentrate as mechanically partially defatted pumpkin seed material followed by pulverizing. Its roasted grade adds light salting and roasting before mechanical partial defatting, then further processing and milling.[8][9]
semantic_review: Original supplier HTML: unroasted protein≥60 moisture≤10 fat≤10; material/process attribution only, unspecified assay basis.
Original supplier HTML: roasted name60 protein≥57 moisture≤8 fat≤17; no batch or roasting-only ranking.

blocks.text: These descriptions distinguish three jobs:
blocks.verdict: editorial heading, interpretation, connective argument or proposed development approach; not an empirical test result

blocks.text:
- **Pressing or mechanical partial defatting** changes the seed material by removing part of its oil.
- **Milling or pulverizing** turns the remaining material into smaller particles. It does not by itself establish how much protein will dissolve.
- **Protein extraction and isolation** can involve dissolving protein under selected conditions, separating solids, precipitating the protein and drying the recovered fraction. The laboratory route discussed below includes those steps after the press cake has already been milled and further de-oiled.[4][8][9]

Original supplier HTML: unroasted protein≥60 moisture≤10 fat≤10; material/process attribution only, unspecified assay basis.

blocks.text: The point is not that every supplier must follow that laboratory route. It is that a retail claim about cold pressing cannot be substituted for evidence about protein isolation, and “finely milled” is not a particle-size distribution or a solubility result.
blocks.verdict: editorial heading, interpretation, connective argument or proposed development approach; not an empirical test result

blocks.text: ## Fine particles and soluble protein are different measurements
blocks.verdict: editorial heading, interpretation, connective argument or proposed development approach; not an empirical test result

blocks.text: ### A laboratory comparison, not a retail mixing test
blocks.verdict: editorial heading, interpretation, connective argument or proposed development approach; not an empirical test result

blocks.text: In a [primary study of pumpkin seed press cake](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC9777787/fullTextXML), researchers started with an already milled 300–600 µm fraction, further de-oiled it with hexane, then extracted protein under alkaline conditions and recovered it by precipitation and freeze-drying. That starting sieve fraction is specific to the experiment—not the mesh specification of any retail powder here.[4]
semantic_review: Original XML methods and table cells reviewed: supernatant/initial protein denominator, half-range versus SD, pooled n=4, pH-specific order, d10 counterexample.

blocks.text: Original Table 1 reports 60.24 ± 0.05 g protein per 100 g untreated press cake and 68.68 ± 0.13 after further de-oiling; fat changes from 13.38 ± 0.12 to 0.77 ± 0.14 g/100 g. These are means ± half deviation range from duplicate measurements, not commercial grade definitions. The comparison illustrates enrichment by removing another component, before the separate protein-isolation stage.[4]
semantic_review: Original XML methods and table cells reviewed: supernatant/initial protein denominator, half-range versus SD, pooled n=4, pH-specific order, d10 counterexample.

blocks.text: The researchers also compared alkaline extraction alone with ultrasound applied before, during or after extraction. Their solubility test used isolated protein at 5 mg/mL, two hours of agitation at room temperature, and centrifugation before measuring protein in the supernatant by Kjeldahl. Solubility here is supernatant protein divided by protein in the initial sample, expressed as a percentage. It was not an instant-drink test.[4]
semantic_review: Original XML methods and table cells reviewed: supernatant/initial protein denominator, half-range versus SD, pooled n=4, pH-specific order, d10 counterexample.

| Ultrasound during alkaline extraction, UAE | 6.59 ± 0.99 d | 18.80 ± 0.52 b | 46.87 ± 0.17 c |
| Ultrasound after alkaline extraction, AE+US | 4.90 ± 0.05 c | 23.07 ± 0.06 c | 46.93 ± 0.61 c |

blocks.text: There is no single winning solubility treatment across these columns: UAE is higher than AE+US at pH 5, AE+US is higher at pH 7, and the two share the same significance group at pH 9. That is more informative than a blanket claim that treating protein after extraction always works best.[4]

blocks.text: The particle results also resist a simple “smaller is better” summary. Original Table 2 gives AE+US the smallest d90, 179.93 µm, but its d10 is 8.05 µm, higher than the control’s 4.82 µm. The measurements describe volume-based particle diameters in dispersions after alkaline extraction, measured at pH 7 after one day at 6°C. They do not characterize retail dry-powder mesh or prove that all parts of the distribution became smaller.[4]
semantic_review: Original XML methods and table cells reviewed: supernatant/initial protein denominator, half-range versus SD, pooled n=4, pH-specific order, d10 counterexample.

blocks.text: ### Preheating does not improve every result
blocks.verdict: editorial heading, interpretation, connective argument or proposed development approach; not an empirical test result

blocks.text: A [second primary study](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC11748320/fullTextXML) separates protein solubility from a water solubility index. Within its alkali-extracted samples, original Table 4 gives protein solubility of 10.32 ± 0.05% for untreated material, 9.75 ± 0.02% after conventional preheating and 15.99 ± 0.04% after microwave preheating (means ± SE, n=3; significance letters c, d and a, respectively). Its general prose suggests preheating improves solubility, but those cells show that conventional preheating did not improve this particular alkali comparison. The water-solubility-index preparation, meanwhile, used a 1:4 sample-to-water ratio and a day of shaking. Neither test establishes consumer mixing speed.[5]
semantic_review: Original XML rowspans and Table4 cells reviewed: Alkali UT10.32 CH9.75 MH15.99, SE n=3; WSI 1:4/day not instant mixing.

blocks.text: Milling can still matter upstream. In a separate [cell-culture-media study](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/nutrition/articles/10.3389/fnut.2025.1602010/full), researchers replaced a heat-generating coffee-grinder preparation with more thorough grinding cooled by liquid nitrogen before protein isolation. They reported higher protein concentrations in the recovered isolates and a changed protein profile. Because grinding intensity and cooling changed together, the experiment cannot isolate a particle-size-only effect; it also cannot validate the mouthfeel or food suitability of a commercial drink powder.[10]
semantic_review: Original publisher HTML concentration/profile findings; grinding/cooling confounded and cell-media application only.

blocks.text: ## Turn the retail promise into a specific development trial
blocks.verdict: editorial heading, interpretation, connective argument or proposed development approach; not an empirical test result

blocks.text: The evidence suggests three different trial briefs, rather than one universal “mixability” score. These are proposed development approaches, not tested recipes:
blocks.verdict: editorial heading, interpretation, connective argument or proposed development approach; not an empirical test result

blocks.text: **For a blender smoothie ingredient**, keep the smoothie base and blending procedure constant while comparing candidate powders. Evaluate flavor, perceived particles and thickening alongside protein contribution. This tests the kitchen-use promise closest to Anthony’s and Micro Ingredients’ positioning, without treating a smoothie as water.[2][3]
semantic_review: Seller kitchen positioning plus toasted/pressed/milled wording; 8g/5g/56 label versus 30 structured field; cold pressing not incompatible with prior toasting.
Seller everyday uses and approximately 30g/18g/30 label; raw/fine-milled not independently measured.

blocks.text: **For a shaker drink**, record wetting, visible lumps and sediment separately. Use a defined serving mass, liquid volume, temperature and shaking procedure. A powder can lose visible lumps yet still settle; the analytical soluble-protein fraction answers a different question from those observations. The laboratory methods above explain why a bare “solubility” number is inadequate without its conditions.[4][5]
semantic_review: Original XML methods and table cells reviewed: supernatant/initial protein denominator, half-range versus SD, pooled n=4, pH-specific order, d10 counterexample.
Original XML rowspans and Table4 cells reviewed: Alkali UT10.32 CH9.75 MH15.99, SE n=3; WSI 1:4/day not instant mixing.

blocks.text: **For a roasted savory or baked concept**, treat flavor as part of the ingredient’s role, not just a defect to mask. Start with the supplier’s actual roasted specification and judge the finished food for color, flavor and texture. Austrade’s description supports this as a plausible development direction, not as an already validated formula or a fixed substitution ratio.[9]
semantic_review: Original supplier HTML: roasted name60 protein≥57 moisture≤8 fat≤17; no batch or roasting-only ranking.

blocks.text: The strongest pumpkin-protein proposition is therefore a matched combination of material description, use occasion and preparation experience. The original listings show how brands frame that combination. Supplier documents and primary experiments show where the wording stops short of technical proof. Keeping those evidence types separate makes the commercial story more useful—not less.
blocks.verdict: editorial heading, interpretation, connective argument or proposed development approach; not an empirical test result

blocks.text: ## 压榨取油、粉碎成粉、提取蛋白，是三件不同的事
blocks.verdict: editorial heading, interpretation, connective argument or proposed development approach; not an empirical test result

blocks.text: 供应商资料可以帮助理解：商品名里的“南瓜籽蛋白”不一定意味着经过纯化的分离蛋白。Austrade 对未烘烤浓缩蛋白的描述是先机械部分脱脂，再粉碎；其烘烤款则先轻度加盐、烘烤，再机械部分脱脂，随后进一步加工和研磨。[8][9]

Original supplier HTML: roasted name60 protein≥57 moisture≤8 fat≤17; no batch or roasting-only ranking.

blocks.text: 由此可以区分三项操作：
blocks.verdict: editorial heading, interpretation, connective argument or proposed development approach; not an empirical test result

blocks.text:
- **压榨或机械部分脱脂**：去掉种籽中的一部分油脂，改变剩余物料的组成。
- **粉碎或研磨**：把物料变成更小的颗粒，但不能单凭这一步判断有多少蛋白能够溶解。
- **蛋白提取与分离**：在选定条件下使蛋白进入液相，再分离固体、沉淀蛋白并干燥回收。下文的实验路线是在饼粕已经研磨、进一步脱油之后，才进行这些操作。[4][8][9]

blocks.text: ### 实验室比较：看懂条件，再看数值

blocks.text: 一项[南瓜籽饼粕原始研究](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC9777787/fullTextXML)，使用已经研磨的300–600微米粒级，先以己烷进一步脱油，再进行碱性提取、沉淀和冷冻干燥。这里的起始粒级只属于这项实验，不能拿来充当本文任何一款零售粉末的粒度规格。[4]
semantic_review: Original XML methods and table cells reviewed: supernatant/initial protein denominator, half-range versus SD, pooled n=4, pH-specific order, d10 counterexample.

blocks.text: 原文表1中，未进一步脱油的饼粕蛋白质为60.24 ± 0.05克/100克，进一步脱油后为68.68 ± 0.13克/100克；脂肪则从13.38 ± 0.12降到0.77 ± 0.14克/100克。这里的“±”是两次测定的半极差，不是标准差。这组数据说明，去掉部分非蛋白成分便能提高蛋白质在剩余物料中的占比；后续的蛋白提取与分离仍是另一个步骤。这些数值也不是商业等级的定义。[4]

blocks.text: 研究者随后比较了单独碱提与在碱提前、碱提中、碱提后加入超声处理的效果。溶解性测试使用5毫克/毫升的分离蛋白，在室温下搅拌两小时，再离心，以凯氏定氮法测上清液中的蛋白。这里的溶解性，是上清液蛋白量占初始样品蛋白量的百分比。这与消费者冲一杯即饮蛋白粉的过程相去甚远。[4]

blocks.text: ### 预热并非在所有条件下都有利
blocks.verdict: editorial heading, interpretation, connective argument or proposed development approach; not an empirical test result

blocks.text: [另一项原始研究](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC11748320/fullTextXML)把“蛋白溶解性”与“水溶性指数”分开测定。其原文表4中，碱提样品未经预热时的蛋白溶解性为10.32 ± 0.05%，常规预热后为9.75 ± 0.02%，微波预热后为15.99 ± 0.04%（均值±标准误，n=3，显著性字母依次为c、d、a）。尽管正文概括性地认为预热有利于溶解，这组单元格却显示：在该碱提比较中，常规预热并没有带来提高。水溶性指数的制样条件又不同，采用样品与水1:4的质量比，并振荡一天。这两种检测都不能直接回答“冲调需要几秒”。[5]
semantic_review: Original XML rowspans and Table4 cells reviewed: Alkali UT10.32 CH9.75 MH15.99, SE n=3; WSI 1:4/day not instant mixing.

blocks.text: 研磨在上游当然可能起作用。一项面向[细胞培养基的研究](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/nutrition/articles/10.3389/fnut.2025.1602010/full)，把会产生明显热量的咖啡研磨机处理，改为液氮冷却下更充分的研磨，然后再分离蛋白；作者报告回收分离物中的蛋白浓度提高，蛋白组成也有所变化。不过，研磨程度和冷却条件同时改变，无法把效果单独归因于粒径。这项研究的用途也不是评价饮料，不能用来证明商业蛋白粉的口感或食品适用性。[10]

blocks.text: ## 把“好用”落实为不同的配方试验
blocks.verdict: editorial heading, interpretation, connective argument or proposed development approach; not an empirical test result

blocks.text: 结合商品定位和实验方法，可以形成三种不同的开发任务，而不是给所有产品打一个笼统的“易溶解”分数。以下是建议的试验方向，并非已经验证的配方。
blocks.verdict: editorial heading, interpretation, connective argument or proposed development approach; not an empirical test result

blocks.text: **如果做搅拌机奶昔用粉**，应固定奶昔基底与搅拌程序，再比较候选粉末。除了蛋白贡献，还要看风味、入口颗粒感和增稠程度。这更接近 Anthony’s 和 Micro Ingredients 所描述的厨房用途，也避免把复杂奶昔当成清水来测试。[2][3]
semantic_review: Seller kitchen positioning plus toasted/pressed/milled wording; 8g/5g/56 label versus 30 structured field; cold pressing not incompatible with prior toasting.
Seller everyday uses and approximately 30g/18g/30 label; raw/fine-milled not independently measured.

blocks.text: **如果做摇摇杯冲饮粉**，应分别记录润湿、可见结团和沉降。每份用量、液体体积、温度以及摇匀方法都要固定。没有明显粉团，并不代表静置后不会沉淀；上清液里测出的蛋白比例，与这些肉眼观察也不是同一个指标。前述论文恰好说明，脱离测试条件的“溶解性”数字很难指导冲调体验。[4][5]
semantic_review: Original XML methods and table cells reviewed: supernatant/initial protein denominator, half-range versus SD, pooled n=4, pH-specific order, d10 counterexample.
Original XML rowspans and Table4 cells reviewed: Alkali UT10.32 CH9.75 MH15.99, SE n=3; WSI 1:4/day not instant mixing.

blocks.text: **如果做烘烤风味的咸味食品或烘焙产品**，可以把原料自身的香味作为配方的一部分，而不只是设法掩盖它。按照具体烘烤款的规格选样，再在成品里判断颜色、风味和质构。Austrade 的描述为这个方向提供了依据，却没有给出已经验证的成品配方或固定替代比例。[9]
semantic_review: Original supplier HTML: roasted name60 protein≥57 moisture≤8 fat≤17; no batch or roasting-only ranking.

blocks.text: 因此，南瓜籽蛋白产品真正需要配合起来的是原料形态、食用场景和制备体验。三个零售样本展示了品牌如何表达这些价值；供应商资料和原始实验则帮助判断，哪些表达已有工艺或数据支持，哪些还需要实际验证。把这些层次分清，才能让产品定位既具体，又经得起追问。

blocks.text: 本文使用2026年9月28日原始 Amazon.com 搜索返回的八条记录，以及三个不同品牌的商品详情。分析时去除了重复要点，原始采集包装文件完整保留。同日后续查看了对应ASIN的初始商品图库，补充了上文标签数据。Sprout 的营养和配料信息来自标签设计图，Anthony’s 与 Micro 则有背袋照片；图库与商品页的对应关系不等于已核验购买实物。供应商规格仍属供应商声明；没有进行购买、批次COA核验、独立认证审核或成品试验。论文数据只对应各自的实验材料，不对应这三款零售商品。本文不作价格、评价数量、市场份额或营养高低排名。
